text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri's government won a parliamentary vote of confidence, 102 MPs voted yea and 19 MPs said no.
-Army troops and police deployed in Beirut to stop planned opposition and labour demonstrations.
-Israeli shelling on villages in south Lebanon.
-German environmental experts examined containers of plastic waste illegally shipped to Beirut.
-Prosecutor General Addoum demanded capital punishment for a Palestininian fundamentalist suspected of assassinating the political leader of an Islamic pro-Syrian group in 1995.
-Lebanon's casino, the biggest amusement center in the Middle East before it closed during the 1975-90 civil war, will reopen on Wednesday.
-Hariri agrees to temporarily extend the deadline for unlicensed radio and television stations to shut down.
-Prime Minister Hariri says Lebanon is in a much better situation than it was four years ago when he first came to office.
